key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset during activity - pivoting, cutting, landing, or direct blow. Common in sports requiring sudden direction changes. LOCATION: Anterior knee, may radiate to posterior knee. DURATION: Immediate severe pain that may worsen over first 24-48 hours. CHARACTER: SHARP initial pain, then THROBBING and ACHING. AGGRAVATING: WEIGHT BEARING, walking, stairs, pivoting, cutting movements. RELIEVING: REST, ICE, elevation, NSAIDs. TIMING: Immediate pain, swelling develops over hours, stiffness increases over 24-48 hours. SEVERITY: 6-9/10, severe with activity. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: SWELLING within hours (effusion), BRUISING develops over 24-48 hours, INSTABILITY (knee 'giving way'), difficulty walking or bearing weight, may have audible 'pop' at injury. KEY POSITIVES: Positive Lachman test, positive anterior drawer test, positive pivot shift test, joint effusion, positive McMurray test (if meniscus involved). KEY NEGATIVES: No bony tenderness over patella or tibial plateau (rules out fracture), no obvious deformity.

red_flags: Severe pain with inability to bear weight - possible associated fracture or severe injury
Severe swelling with severe pain - possible hemarthrosis or severe ligament injury
Severe pain with neurological deficits - possible nerve injury, needs urgent evaluation
Severe pain with fever - possible infection, needs urgent evaluation
Severe pain with night pain - possible malignancy, needs urgent evaluation
